stories.title: BlackRock says AI agents could drive stablecoin and crypto adoption
stories.summary: BlackRock published commentary saying autonomous AI agents may become major users of stablecoins and other crypto assets. The firm argues that agents need machine-native payment rails to transact on their own. CryptoSlate described the opportunity as a possible $5 trillion trade, while Cointelegraph noted BlackRock called this demand driver "underappreciated."
stories.whyItMatters: A push from the world's largest asset manager into the AI-agent payments narrative could shape how institutions design and adopt stablecoin products.
whatToWatch: Watch for BlackRock product filings tied to stablecoins or AI-agent payments.
Watch for other asset managers echoing this thesis.
questions: How would AI agents actually hold and spend stablecoins in practice?
What rules would govern payments initiated by an autonomous agent?

stories.title: NYSE and Blockchain.com to bring tokenized US stocks to crypto users
stories.summary: NYSE and crypto exchange Blockchain.com are working together to bring tokenized versions of US stocks to crypto users, per Cointelegraph and Bitcoin Magazine. The tie-up would let crypto platform users trade tokenized equities alongside digital assets. Early reports gave few details on launch timing or structure.
stories.whyItMatters: A partnership between a major US stock exchange and a crypto exchange could speed up mainstream tokenization of traditional securities.
whatToWatch: Watch for a formal announcement with a launch date.
Watch for which stocks get tokenized first and under what regulatory approval.
questions: What regulatory approvals does tokenized stock trading need?
Will other exchanges strike similar deals?

stories.title: Dogecoin down 8%, bitcoin under $84,000 as Treasury yields hit 2007 high
stories.summary: Dogecoin fell about 8% and bitcoin dropped below $84,000 as US Treasury yields reached their highest level since 2007, per CoinDesk. Rising yields make traditional, lower-risk assets more attractive relative to volatile crypto. CoinDesk tied the crypto selloff directly to this bond-market move.
stories.whyItMatters: The selloff shows how closely crypto prices now track broader macro conditions like interest rates, not just crypto-specific news.
whatToWatch: Watch for further moves in Treasury yields.
Watch for whether bitcoin holds support near current levels.
questions: How much further could yields rise from here?
Will crypto keep tracking rates moves, or decouple again?

stories.title: Kalshi says CFTC hasn't contacted it over unusual $5B trading activity
stories.summary: Prediction market Kalshi said the CFTC has not contacted it about a reported $5 billion in "unusual" trading activity on its platform. The statement pushes back on suggestions that regulators are investigating the company. Both CoinDesk and Cointelegraph reported Kalshi's denial.
stories.whyItMatters: Prediction markets sit at the edge of crypto and regulated derivatives, so any CFTC scrutiny here could set a precedent for the sector.
whatToWatch: Watch for any formal CFTC statement or inquiry.
Watch for details on what made the trading activity "unusual."
questions: What exactly was flagged as unusual?
Could the CFTC still open a review despite Kalshi's denial?

stories.whyItMatters: The death of a prominent crypto VC figure, following a public dispute with her firm, is drawing attention across the industry.
whatToWatch: Watch for any statement from Hack VC.
Watch for further reporting on the circumstances of her death.

stories.title: EU watchdogs warn quantum computers could break crypto's security
stories.summary: EU financial watchdogs warned that future quantum computers could eventually break the cryptographic protections that secure crypto assets and other digital systems, per Cointelegraph. The warning describes a longer-term risk, not an imminent threat. It calls for preparation toward quantum-resistant cryptography.
stories.whyItMatters: If quantum computing advances faster than the shift to quantum-resistant systems, it could threaten the security of existing wallets and blockchains.
whatToWatch: Watch for EU guidance on post-quantum migration timelines.
Watch for major blockchains announcing quantum-resistant upgrades.
questions: How soon could quantum computers pose a real threat?
Which blockchains and wallets are most exposed?

stories.title: Circle launches 24/7 stablecoin FX engine to chase the $10 trillion currency market
stories.summary: Circle launched a stablecoin-based foreign exchange engine that runs 24 hours a day, seven days a week, per CryptoSlate. The move targets a slice of the roughly $10 trillion daily currency trading market. It positions Circle's stablecoins as a settlement rail for round-the-clock FX trades.
stories.whyItMatters: A working stablecoin FX rail could pull real trading volume from traditional currency markets into crypto infrastructure.
whatToWatch: Watch for adoption numbers or partner announcements.
Watch for rival stablecoin issuers launching similar products.
questions: Which counterparties or exchanges will use the engine first?
How will it handle compliance across different jurisdictions?

stories.title: MoonPay to acquire SEC-registered North Capital in $60 million all-stock deal
stories.summary: MoonPay agreed to acquire North Capital, an SEC-registered broker-dealer, in an all-stock deal worth more than $60 million. The deal gives MoonPay a regulated entity for securities-related work. Both CoinDesk and Cointelegraph reported the terms.
stories.whyItMatters: Buying a registered broker-dealer lets a crypto payments firm move further into tokenized securities and other regulated products.
whatToWatch: Watch for the deal's close date and any regulatory review.
Watch for MoonPay's plans for North Capital's licenses.

stories.title: China probes DeepSeek and Moonshot over alleged data leaks to Anthropic's Claude

stories.whyItMatters: The probe highlights rising scrutiny of cross-border AI data flows, a backdrop to the broader AI-crypto convergence story this lane also tracks.
whatToWatch: Watch for official statements from Chinese regulators.

stories.title: Ex-SEC acting chair says agency dropped crypto cases to protect its credibility
stories.summary: A former SEC acting chair said the agency dropped certain crypto enforcement cases to avoid damaging its own credibility, per Cointelegraph. The comment adds to ongoing debate over the SEC's shifting approach to crypto enforcement. The report did not name specific dropped cases.
stories.whyItMatters: Comments from a former top SEC official suggest internal doubts about past crypto enforcement decisions, which could shape future policy.
whatToWatch: Watch for reaction from current SEC leadership.
Watch for any cases that get reopened or referenced directly.
questions: Which cases were dropped, and why?
